metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 produced all seven required todo/write snapshots in a seven-turn live recording. The DSH parser skips those records, so task_delta remains absent and the session API tasks field cannot populate.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: bug
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 has the exact single-session task-list feature. The installed TUI composition includes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo` with `allowParallelInProgress: true`. Its official package documentation and installed implementation define the model-facing `todo_write` tool as a whole-list replacement over items `{content,status}`, where status is `pending`, `in_progress`, or `completed`. Every successful call appends a durable `todo/write` record to the calling agent session. The tool rejects calls without an owning agent session. It does not create a child session. This satisfies the agent pillar and keeps SubagentCount at 0 when the recipe uses only `todo_write`.

The daemon has a parser bug for the load-bearing task observable. `core/adapters/inbound/agents/dsh/parser.go` has handlers for turn, approval, message, tool, and request records, but no handler for `todo/write`. `ParseLine` marks every unknown record skipped. The generic `tool/call` handler keeps only `callId` and `name`; it does not decode the todo arguments. The parser therefore emits neither `TaskDeltas` nor a `TaskSnapshot`. The tailer cannot populate `SessionMetrics.Tasks`, and the session API `tasks` field remains empty even though the durable transcript contains every full task snapshot. This is `daemon=bug`, not `incapable`, because the official tool implementation explicitly writes the complete signal into the local session log that the DSH Source tails.

The other required signals are observable. The parser maps `turn/start` to working and completed `turn/end` to ready. A `todo_write` call is handled inside the same agent session and needs no permission approval. The spec asserts the correct task behavior with seven durable `todo/write` snapshots, one for each required status transition. It also asserts a `task_delta` daemon event. That phase is known failing until the parser maps the snapshots through `tailer.TodoReconciler`.

The recipe needs only `send`, `wait_turn`, and `sleep`. The DeepSeek Harness driver implements all three. The 10-second trailing sleep matches the longest committed sibling delay for this scenario. The 600-second timeout covers seven local model/tool rounds. The settings pin the same locally measured model and endpoint as the existing DeepSeek Harness cells.

## Vacuous-pass check

This cell could pass without testing the current run if the driver reused a prior transcript that already contained the same seven snapshots. The fresh per-run cwd, pre-launch marker, header-cwd match, and session-ID contract are therefore load-bearing recipe preconditions.

## Live recording confirmation

The seven-turn recording 2026-09-19-05-12-27_irrlichd-0.6.4+03d0073 contains all seven exact todo/write states and seven completed turns. `go run ./tools/onboarding-factory/cmd/of verify --agent deepseek-harness --scenario task-list --json` reports 13/13 transcript assertions and 2/2 event assertions passing. The task_tracked state phase alone fails (5/6 phases) because the parser still skips todo/write. This is a daemon parser gap, not a source-fixture miss.
caveats: KNOWN FAILING: the DSH parser has no todo/write handler and its generic tool/call handler drops arguments, so it emits no TaskDelta or TaskSnapshot and the session API tasks field stays empty.

LIVE 2.3 recording 2026-09-19-05-12-27_irrlichd-0.6.4+03d0073 confirms all seven exact todo/write snapshots and seven tool/call records. The sole failing phase is task_tracked: the DSH parser emits no TaskDelta or TaskSnapshot from todo/write.
todo_write is full-list replacement. A fix must reconcile each authoritative snapshot, including removals and status reversions, instead of treating each record as an independent create.
Load-bearing environment precondition: the active TUI profile must still mount @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo. Re-probe `dsh --profile tui --dump-config` at record time.
Load-bearing environment precondition: LM Studio must serve qwen/qwen3.5-9b at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1. The exact model observation and the recipe depend on this endpoint.

Vacuous-pass condition: reuse of a prior matching transcript could prove nothing about the current run. The driver must keep its fresh per-run cwd, pre-launch marker, header-cwd match, and resolved session-ID contract.

sources.note: Official package documentation: todo_write replaces the whole list, supports pending/in_progress/completed, appends todo/write to the owning agent session, and has no shared or subagent scope.
Installed 0.1.5-rc.2 implementation: registers todo_write and executes exec.agent.session.append('todo/write', { todos }).
Active profile inspected with `dsh --profile tui --dump-config`: mounts @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo with allowParallelInProgress=true.
recordHandlers has no todo/write entry; unknown records are skipped, and parseToolCall preserves only callId and name with no task extraction.
Shared full-list reconciliation path that produces TaskDeltas and TaskSnapshot for adapters with todo snapshots; the DSH parser does not call it.
Session tasks and task_delta lifecycle events are produced only from parser-emitted TaskDeltas and TaskSnapshot data.
Declares and implements send, wait_turn, and sleep; resolves a readable post-marker transcript whose header cwd matches the fresh run cwd.

preconditions: dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 or newer is installed and on PATH
the active TUI profile mounts @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo; re-probe with `dsh --profile tui --dump-config` at record time
LM Studio is listening at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 with qwen/qwen3.5-9b loaded
irrlichd is recording with DeepSeek Harness transcript permission granted
the driver uses its fresh per-run cwd and pre-launch transcript marker
setup: The interactive driver creates a fresh cwd under staging and launches `dsh --profile tui` in tmux.
The driver applies a temporary patch that selects LM Studio and qwen/qwen3.5-9b without modifying the installed TUI profile.
The driver resolves only a readable post-marker session.v3.jsonl.zstd whose session header cwd matches the run cwd.

script.text: For this turn, call only the todo_write tool. Call it exactly once with this complete argument: {"todos":[{"content":"draft a greeting","status":"pending"},{"content":"refine the greeting","status":"pending"},{"content":"reply done","status":"pending"}]}. This is the initial all-pending snapshot. Keep every item and status exactly as shown. Do not call any other tool. After the tool result, reply only DONE.

For this turn, call only the todo_write tool. Call it exactly once with this complete argument: {"todos":[{"content":"draft a greeting","status":"in_progress"},{"content":"refine the greeting","status":"pending"},{"content":"reply done","status":"pending"}]}. This is the first in-progress snapshot. Keep every item and status exactly as shown. Do not call any other tool. After the tool result, reply only DONE.

For this turn, call only the todo_write tool. Call it exactly once with this complete argument: {"todos":[{"content":"draft a greeting","status":"completed"},{"content":"refine the greeting","status":"pending"},{"content":"reply done","status":"pending"}]}. This is the first completed snapshot. Keep every item and status exactly as shown. Do not call any other tool. After the tool result, reply only DONE.

For this turn, call only the todo_write tool. Call it exactly once with this complete argument: {"todos":[{"content":"draft a greeting","status":"completed"},{"content":"refine the greeting","status":"in_progress"},{"content":"reply done","status":"pending"}]}. This is the second in-progress snapshot. Keep every item and status exactly as shown. Do not call any other tool. After the tool result, reply only DONE.

For this turn, call only the todo_write tool. Call it exactly once with this complete argument: {"todos":[{"content":"draft a greeting","status":"completed"},{"content":"refine the greeting","status":"completed"},{"content":"reply done","status":"pending"}]}. This is the second completed snapshot. Keep every item and status exactly as shown. Do not call any other tool. After the tool result, reply only DONE.

For this turn, call only the todo_write tool. Call it exactly once with this complete argument: {"todos":[{"content":"draft a greeting","status":"completed"},{"content":"refine the greeting","status":"completed"},{"content":"reply done","status":"in_progress"}]}. This is the third in-progress snapshot. Keep every item and status exactly as shown. Do not call any other tool. After the tool result, reply only DONE.

For this turn, call only the todo_write tool. Call it exactly once with this complete argument: {"todos":[{"content":"draft a greeting","status":"completed"},{"content":"refine the greeting","status":"completed"},{"content":"reply done","status":"completed"}]}. This is the all completed snapshot. Keep every item and status exactly as shown. Do not call any other tool. After the tool result, reply only DONE.

verify: the compressed transcript contains seven todo/write snapshots that walk the three exact items from all pending through each separate in_progress and completed state
the transcript contains no subagent, subagent_fork, or workflow tool call and events.jsonl contains no parent_linked event, so SubagentCount stays 0
events.jsonl shows the real session-UUID row moving ready -> working -> ready with no waiting transition
KNOWN FAILING: events.jsonl contains at least one task_delta and the session API tasks field lists the three exact items as completed
the recording reports model qwen/qwen3.5-9b and non-zero tokens
recipe.scope_note: Seven separate DSH turns force one full-list todo_write snapshot per required state. This addresses the first live recording, which skipped the first-completed and second-completed snapshots when asked to perform the full walk in one turn. The 600-second timeout and 10-second trailing settle delay remain.
